steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Lightly grease or line 10 muffin cups.

In a medium bowl, combine eggs and bananas. In a separate bowl, mix together flour, salt, sugar and baking soda. Stir banana mixture into flour mixture. Fold in walnuts if desired. Pour batter into prepared muffin cups.
Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into center of a muffin comes out clean.

raw_recipe.headline: Lighter Banana Muffins
raw_recipe.description: There is no oil or butter in these muffins, but they are still rich and moist -with eggs and all that banana, how could they not be? So gobble them up with a clear conscience!
raw_recipe.name: Lighter Banana Muffins

Bake in preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into center of a muffin comes out clean.

review.reviewBody: These muffins were very yummy and moist, and surprisingly fat free. Many people said their muffins came out a little dry so I added an extra banana and 1/4 cup of skim milk. Also, I used 1 cup of whole wheat flour and 1 cup of white and added some cinnamon and vanilla. I replaced white sugar with brown sugar and I found that 3/4 cups of sugar was too sweet for my taste so I would reduce it to 1/2 cup next time. Overall, the muffins were delicious and I would definitely make them again.

I halved the recipe as I only had 4 medium sized banana. I also added half a teaspoon of baking powder, to which I'm glad because my 6 muffins rose beautifully. I filled about 2/3 of each silicon muffin cups, which I did not grease. Mine came out like flavorful banana bread instead of the usual muffins that I made, probably because I overmixed the batter, which I could have avoided if I added milk or applesauce, as there were bits of flour that were unmixed (but once the batter were clear of flour bits, it was just nice - not too thick or runny). 

I was worried this would come out dry/burnt but it didn't, I think the key is OVERRIPE bananas - the ones I used were too soft to peel and eat, but were still good/edible enough for baking. I imagine if I used firm bananas these would turn out dense and dry like some other reviewers noted. I will make these again only if I have overripe bananas on hand (and next time I'll sprinkle some brown sugar on top because I like a good crust, and these came out too light/yellow for me)

Followed the original recipe with these changes:
 1. 4 bananas (instead of 3) smashed with 4oz of applesauce and 1 tsp vanilla (along with the eggs required for recipe)
2. 1 cup whole wheat flour and 1 cup all purpose flour 
3. No white sugar, use 1/2 cup brown sugar 
4. Add 1 tsp cinnamon 
Try sticking a toothpick in the muffins after 20 minutes in the oven, mine are fully cooked at this point and super moist.

I think this was a great recipe because it was good and versatile. I used this as a base recipe and then made several minor changes and it still came out great, without difficulty.

I put in 1C white flour and 1C oat flour. I added 1/2 tsp cinn. and 1 tsp vanilla. I used previously frozen bananas and only 1/2 C sugar. (The taste test at that point was fine.) Then, I added 5T of a blueberry/plum sauce I made a few days earlier (blueberries, plums, water, sugar and lemon juice). 

Don't feel you have to do all that, I just had them on hand and felt like experimenting. I like the contrasting taste, since it was a bit tart.

Because I used previously frozen bananas and the berry sauce, I didn't have any problems with the batter being too dry. It wasn't overly sweet, and at the end of the day, only 3 of the 14 remain. (Our landlord, who traditionally refuses sweets, not only ate two, but readily took two to go.) Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

Had to modify out of necessity: Used 4 ripe bananas, 2 c. plus 2 TBSP self-rising flour, no salt , no baking soda, Added 1/2 c. applesauce, used 1/2 c. brown sugar (plus a little for the top with the spice), added 2 tsp Penzey's Pie Spice ( a blend of cinnamon,mace, ginger, nutmeg, anise seed and clove). 1/2 tsp vanilla. Sprinkle top with a shake of spice and a dab brown sugar. Made 12 full muffins, in a greased tin, they rise nicely. They are excellent. IF I could have nuts they'd have been better yet. Great recipe, thanks!

Once I adapted the recipe, they were GREAT and I plan to use the recipe again! Having taken into account suggestions from previous reviews, I made the following changes : added 1/4 of 2% milk, 1/2 cup of 0% fat Greek yoghurt (I had no apple sauce) only brown sugar, 1/2 cup of walnut pieces (quantity hadn’t been specified) and 2.5 tsp of pumpkin spice. Muffins were awesome -nice and moist!

I tried this recipe using Quick cooking Mother's oats grinded down to flour texture (using Bella rocket blender), adding 1t. cornstarch as a binder and 1/4 c. Pure maple syrup as sugar substitute. Very tasty and moist, almost similar to a bran muffin...but better!

I followed the suggestions of other reviewers and used three egg whites, four bananas, 1/4 cup skim milk, and a dash of vanilla in the wet ingredients. For the dry I used 1 cup white flour, 1/2 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup rolled oats, 1/2 cup brown sugar, and dash nutmeg (along the with salt and baking soda the recipe calls for.) Once I filled 12 muffin liners, I sprinkled cinnamon and brown sugar on top before baking. I will probably make these again, though I will up the sugar slightly.

I did what others suggested, and used 1/2 cup applesauce, 1 tsp cinnamon, and 1 tsp vanilla. I only had 3 bananas though-came out perfectly! I left the muffins overnight in a covered container-must do this!! I woke up and they were SUPER moist!! Highly recommend this recipe.

I just made this recipe and the muffins are delicious. I followed the advice of other's here and added 4oz unsweetened applesauce, 4 bananas, 1 tsp of vanilla and 1 tsp of cinnamon, used less sugar (a little more than 1/2 cup) but changed up the flour (I used 1 cup all-purpose flour and 1 cup spelt flour) and added sliced almonds to the top with a little sprinkling of brown sugar. My only dislike was that the outside of the muffin stuck to the paper .....so I am thinking next time I will just eliminate the paper muffin cups and spray the tin.

Great recipe! I followed the original recipe and added a few things... I used 5 bananas (instead of 3), added 1 tsp of cinnamon to the flour/sugar mixture, and added 1 tsp vanilla and 1/4 cup cinnamon apple sauce to the banana/egg mixture. I also sprinkled on light brown sugar to the tops of the muffin halfway during baking!! So delicious!!! YUM YUM! I will be making again!! :)
Absolutely perfect, delicious. I have eaten three already and they only came out of the oven half an hour ago!!

2025 review, i added a tsp of vanilla extract & a cup of apple sauce and topped with crushed walnuts and oh my god... rhese were fantastic.. i ate 5 in one sitting... i am very judgemental and the reviews honestly scared me. these were perfect. i didnt do that much salt . & also added cinnamon and pumpkin pie spice. my house smelled amazing.
Eh they lacked flavor and were very heavy
I would use a little less salt I think and maybe add some cinnamon. They have good flavor and texture, they’re just a little salty for me.
I read some of the reviews and I added some milk! Soo glad I did! I used frozen berries, cinnamon and a little bit of sugar! I think 20 mins is the ideal time!

They turned out nicely with a dense and somewhat spongey texture. They are soft with a prominent banana flavor. I used 4 small to medium size bananas and added walnuts; I got 12 muffins. I greased a muffin tin and had no problems with sticking to the pan. The bottoms and edges are darker than typical muffins, but they didn't burn. The next day they are a bit heavier, but still soft and taste good. They are best warmed up.

Thank you for this recipe as it made me getting back in my kitchen after a year of no cooking easier. I love cooking , but covid put my mixer on the shelf. The baking of these muffins filled my kitchen with a delightful smell of banana. I didn't have baking soda so I substituted 4 teaspoons of baking powder and instead of white sugar I used Morena pure cane sugar. I followed instructions and yielded 15 muffins.
This is a very tasty muffin recipe. I do add cinnamon as personal choice. Muffins are not oily or overly sweet.
